## Open flags

- Validation set is small, so metrics carry wide intervals. Use the CIs.
- Random split only. No company id or year exists, so a time-based split is impossible.
- Attr21 (sales_growth) needs last year's sales, and it is the second strongest feature.
- The test split was read once, in Phase 5, and is locked. Nothing may be tuned on it. Any further model change needs new data.
- Validation has only 61 bankrupt firms and ECE uses 10 equal-frequency bins of about 87 firms (about 6 positives each), so ECE and the reliability points are noisy. Read them with the CIs.
- Calibrators and bands were fitted on 5-fold out-of-fold scores of the train split (286 bankrupt). The saved models are refit on all of train, so they are slightly stronger than the fold models the calibrators saw. Direction of the bias is not verified.
- Cost ratios 5:1, 10:1 and 20:1 are assumptions, not estimates from any lender or data.
- Band cuts are fitted on validation by user instruction, so validation precision and recall at the cuts are in-sample and optimistic. The independent check is the same cuts applied to train out-of-fold scores.
- The High precision floor 0.60 was set after an earlier precision-floor diagnostic and the validation tradeoff table had been seen, so it is not a blind choice.
- logistic_regression: recall of the flagged bands on train OOF (0.797) is below the 0.80 target the cut reached on validation.
- logistic_regression: isotonic gives exactly 0 or 1 to 19 validation firms (log loss clips at 0.0001), which is overconfident and costs log loss.
- lightgbm: recall of the flagged bands on train OOF (0.769) is below the 0.80 target the cut reached on validation.
- lightgbm: the Watch band is thin (16 validation firms with 4 bankrupt, 52 train OOF firms), because the 80% recall cut (0.1736) and the precision cut (0.2403) are close. Its rate rests on very few positives.
- lightgbm: isotonic gives exactly 0 or 1 to 151 validation firms (log loss clips at 0.0001), which is overconfident and costs log loss.
- neural_net: High-band precision on train OOF (0.575) is below the 0.60 floor the cut reached on validation.
- neural_net: isotonic gives exactly 0 or 1 to 33 validation firms (log loss clips at 0.0001), which is overconfident and costs log loss.
- Phase 5: The Watch band is thin on test (16 firms, 3 bankrupt), so its rate carries almost no information. Fewer than 30 firms is the thin-band line.
- Phase 5: neural_net has a higher test PR AUC (0.803) than the headline model (0.797). The intervals overlap almost completely, so neither model can be called better on this test set. By protocol it is reference only and does not replace the headline; the user may choose to revisit.
- Phase 5: Change in PR AUC from validation to test: lightgbm +0.014, logistic_regression +0.121, neural_net +0.081. The models do not move together by the same amount, so the validation gaps between the three models should not be over-read.
- Phase 5: The headline PR AUC is higher on test than on validation. That is the opposite of the expected-optimism direction stated before the run, so the optimism sources do not explain this gap. It is small against the interval width, and the most plausible reading is sampling noise.
- Phase 5: One test set of 61 bankrupt firms. Every interval is wide, and this is a single draw, not a repeated trial.
- Phase 5: Random split only, no company id or year, so this says nothing about performance on future years.
- Phase 5: Calibrators and band cuts were fitted on fold models, while the scored model is refit on all of train. The test run does not isolate this mismatch.
- Phase 5: Attr21 (sales_growth) needs last year's sales, and it is the second strongest feature.
- Phase 5: Nothing was retrained, recalibrated or re-cut after seeing these results, by protocol.
- Phase 6: SHAP describes what the model does, not what causes bankruptcy. A large contribution is a model pattern, not a cause.
- Phase 6: Correlated ratios split credit, so one ratio can look less important because a close twin shares its signal. Known near twins: Attr2 and Attr17 (exact reciprocals), Attr9 and Attr36 (near duplicates). Category sums are only a partial remedy.
- Phase 6: The five categories are assigned by this project from each formula. They are not in the UCI description or the dictionary. Borderline cases are Attr27, Attr30, Attr33, Attr34, Attr37 and Attr58. The full map is in the appendix.
- Phase 6: 3 of the 10 most important features have UNVERIFIED definitions (Attr24, Attr38, Attr13). Read their plain-language names as the UCI wording, which the dictionary marks as possibly mistranslated, unclear or inconsistent.
- Phase 6: Importance stability: Spearman correlation of mean |SHAP| between train and validation is 0.999, and 10 of the top 10 features agree. Agreement with LightGBM gain importance (Spearman) is 0.831.
- Phase 6: Cross-checks: SHAP additivity error against the model output is at most 2.1e-14. The shap library differs from LightGBM's native contributions by at most 0.0e+00; a difference of exactly zero suggests the library delegates to LightGBM's own routine for this model type, so that comparison is not an independent check.
- Phase 6: The frozen model is refit on all of train, while the Platt slope was fitted on fold models. The slope is applied to the refit model. Whether that mismatch matters is not verified.
- Phase 6: The base value is the model's average output over the training trees, not the observed bankruptcy rate, so it need not equal the prevalence.
- Phase 6: Example firms were chosen by a rule fixed in advance, and there is no company id, so they are identified by validation row number.
- Phase 6: Validation has 61 bankrupt firms and importance is an average over all 878 firms. The intervals show the sampling noise.
- Phase 6: Test split untouched in this phase.
- Phase 6: In 2 of the 3 example firms (highest_scoring_true_positive, highest_scoring_false_alarm) the largest driver is Attr21 being missing. The model gives such firms a very large score on that signal alone.
- Phase 6: Attr21 missing vs present SHAP: mean abs SHAP is 5.190 when missing vs 0.322 when present (validation; 12 firms have it missing). Pattern only.
- Phase 6: Attr21 train: bankruptcy rate 0.973 when missing (73 firms) vs 0.053 when present (4021 firms); the 95% Wilson intervals do not overlap. Pattern only.
- Phase 6: Attr21 val: bankruptcy rate 0.917 when missing (12 firms) vs 0.058 when present (866 firms); the 95% Wilson intervals do not overlap. Pattern only.
- Phase 7: Attr21 is missing for 73 train and 12 validation firms, and 71 and 11 of them are bankrupt. Those firms are 24.8% (train) and 18.0% (validation) of all bankrupt firms. In this data, a missing Attr21 almost always goes with a bankrupt label. The cause is not known.
- Phase 7: The validation group is only 12 firms (1 healthy), so anything measured on it is very noisy. Train has the larger group but the model was fit on it, so out-of-fold scores are used for the train performance numbers.
- Phase 7: High band composition on validation: 12 of 75 High firms have Attr21 missing; on train out-of-fold: 73 of 307.
- Phase 7: On firms with Attr21 present, validation PR AUC is 0.713 (0.600 to 0.815) against 0.783 (0.697 to 0.863) for all firms, and train out-of-fold PR AUC is 0.694 against 0.800. The Phase 2 retrain without Attr21 scored 0.687 against 0.783 with it.
- Phase 7: What-if on the frozen model (validation): blanking Attr21 for the 866 firms that have it moves 800 firms to a different band (mean change +5.77 calibrated log-odds). Filling the 12 missing firms with the train median moves 7 firms (mean change -5.01). A user who leaves Attr21 blank gets the model's missing-value behaviour, not a neutral score.
- Phase 7: Co-missingness (train): Attr21-missing firms have a median of 2 attributes missing (mean 3.00, pulled up by a few firms with many missing), against a median of 0 (mean 0.73) for the others. The distribution is in the table.
- Phase 7: For firms with Attr21 present, High-band precision is 0.540 on validation and 0.585 on train out-of-fold, against 0.600 and 0.678 for all firms. The headline numbers are flattered by the small group where a missing value goes with the bankrupt label.
- Phase 7: The dataset has no company id and no year, and no field says why a value is missing. This report states counts and patterns only.
- Phase 7: The test split cannot be broken down by Attr21 status without reading it again, so no such breakdown exists. The Phase 5 test results are unchanged and already include whatever reliance on Attr21 the model has.
- Phase 7: Out-of-fold scores use the saved Platt calibrator that was fitted on those same out-of-fold scores, so the calibrated train numbers are mildly optimistic.
- Phase 7: Test split untouched in this phase. No model, calibrator or cut was changed.
- Phase 8: Blanks in other attributes can carry signal too. In train, a blank Attr27 adds more than 1.0 calibrated log-odds on average to that attribute's contribution. The app's warning therefore also shows the train and validation history for each blank attribute. 2 of the 3 demo firms have a blank attribute. This is descriptive and is not a test of the effect.
- Phase 8: A blank-attribute warning will appear for about half of scorable firms: 47.0% of train and 50.8% of validation firms with Attr21 present have at least one other blank, most often Attr37 (42.3% of train firms). The limit of 6 would block 39 train and 10 validation firms. The effect of these blanks on the score is untested.
- Phase 8: The cuts were set on all firms. High precision on firms with Attr21 present is 0.540 on validation and 0.585 on train out-of-fold, against 0.600 and 0.678 for all firms, and the band rule's floor is 0.60. Nothing was re-cut or recalibrated.
- Phase 8: Calibration on firms with Attr21 present is report only: mean predicted probability 0.0680 against an observed rate of 0.0577 on validation, and 0.0543 against 0.0535 on train out-of-fold. ECE is 0.0134 (0.0082 to 0.0257) on validation and 0.0042 (0.0029 to 0.0101) out-of-fold. Bootstrap ECE is biased upward on small data, so the point estimate can sit outside its own interval.
- Phase 8: Validation Watch band on firms with Attr21 present has 16 firms, so its rate carries very little information.
- Phase 8: Train out-of-fold scores use the saved Platt calibrator that was fitted on those same scores, so the out-of-fold calibration numbers are mildly optimistic.
- Phase 8: The validation cuts were fitted on validation, so validation precision and recall at the cuts are in-sample. Train out-of-fold is the independent check.
- Phase 8: Sector composition of the Polish data is not stated on the UCI page, so the sector is UNVERIFIED. The data is a random split, with no company id or year.
- Phase 8: Test split untouched in this phase. No model, calibrator or cut was changed.
- Phase 9: 13 attributes are blank in at least 20 Attr21-present train firms. 2 meet all three pre-registered criteria: Attr24, Attr27. Under the null, 0.00 would be expected by chance (1000 label permutations). Validation is reused, so these are not described as validated.
- Phase 9: Coverage ceiling CROSSED (train: new refusals hold 31.6% of Attr21-present bankrupt firms (ceiling 30%); val: new refusals hold 38.0% of Attr21-present bankrupt firms (ceiling 30%)). The phase stops after this report and the app is unchanged. Decision: stopped: coverage ceiling crossed, user decides.
- Phase 9: Count limit of 6: the 3 to 6 group does not meet the pre-registered condition, the limit stays at 6.
- Phase 9: Attr27 blank, ridge regression with 53 low-blank covariates: odds ratio 20.35 (14.59 to 36.21), 52 rows dropped. An association only, it does not feed the rule.
- Phase 9: A blocked blank is a guard against trusting a score driven by a blank. It is not a claim that the model is wrong on those firms: see the observed rate against the mean predicted probability among blank firms in the table.
- Phase 9: The test split is spent, so no rule change can be checked on untouched data. Blanks in real use are probably not random like these.
- Phase 9: Test split untouched in this phase. No model, calibrator or cut was changed.
